main_text.p: ideo super Ethnicos, quorum deserti &c solitudinis instar incultus horridusque est animus, se Spiritum suum Sanctum effusurum dicens, ut illuminentur, convertantur cœlestibusque donis perfundantur, Iudæi: quod ipsum alibi quoque docet dicens:Egeni &c pauperes Israelis,quaeEsaj. 41. 17.runt aquas refrigerij, seu auxilium divinum, &c non sunt; lingua eorum siti periit: ego Dominus exaudiam eos. Aperiam in excelsis flumina Spiritus Sancti, &c in medio camporum fontes: ponam desertum Ethnicorum in stagnum aquarum, &c terram solitudinis in scaturigines aquarum (Spiritualium) ut videant Iudæi &c cognoscant, &c ponant super cor, &c intelligant pariter, quod manus Domini fecit istud, &c Sanctus Israelis creavit ipsum. Idem alio Prophetæ hujus loco, sub figurato loquendi modo proponitur. Quum enim prima conversione judæorum, draco ille magnus, qui seducebat tum temporis, uno Ethnicismi errore orbem terrarum, visitatus fuerit: &c jam ad hunc qui in insulis tantum remotis adhuc dominatur, duo serpentes leviathan accesserit: unus Paparum tortuosus, qui callide variis dolis Ecclesiam aggreditur:

page.notes: The marginal reference "Esaj. 41. 17." is printed in the left margin beside the line "runt aquas"; it is placed at the point in the text where it stands. Page number read as "132" from the printed "13Ƨ" at the head. Long s has been transcribed as plain s throughout, including "deserti" and "instar" where the scan shows the long form. The printed "Paparum" and "Ethnicismi" are left as printed. The printed hyphen in "quae-runt" and "ag-greditur" is kept. The final "greditur:" line carries the printed colon.
